founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֹתִ֗י דֶּ֣רֶךְ שַׁ֤עַר הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ הַֽחִיצ֔וֹן הַפֹּנֶ֖ה קָדִ֑ים וְה֖וּא סָגֽוּר׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east; and it was shut.

notes.official: *šaʿar hammiqdāš haḥîṣôn* 'the outer gate of the sanctuary', *hap̄ōneh qāḏîm* 'which faces east', *wəhûʾ sāḡûr* 'and it was shut'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהוָ֗ה הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַזֶּה֩ סָג֨וּר יִהְיֶ֜ה לֹ֣א יִפָּתֵ֗חַ וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא־יָ֣בֹא ב֔וֹ כִּ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣א ב֑וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה סָגֽוּר׃

i18n.en: YHWH said to me, "This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it, for YHWH, the Elohim of Israel, has entered by it; and it shall be shut.

notes.official:
*haššaʿar hazzeh sāḡûr yihyeh lōʾ yippāṯēaḥ* 'This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened': the reason is that 'YHWH, the Elohim of Israel, has entered by it' (43:1-4) (`elohei-yisrael`). The speech runs to v 3.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('This gate shall be shut ... because Yahweh, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it') and comments that the creators did not want to be disturbed. The line renders the verse lexically.

paragraphs.text: אֶֽת־הַנָּשִׂ֗יא נָ֥שִׂיא ה֛וּא יֵֽשֶׁב־בּ֥וֹ לֶאֱכָול־לֶ֖חֶם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ אֻלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

i18n.en: As for the prince, as prince he shall sit in it to eat bread before YHWH; by the way of the porch of the gate he shall enter, and by the same way he shall go out."

notes.official:
*ʾeṯ-hannāśîʾ nāśîʾ hûʾ yēšeḇ-bô* is awkward syntax, literally 'As for the prince — prince he is — he shall sit in it'. The line follows the ASV construal, 'as prince he shall sit in it'. *nāśîʾ* 'prince' is Ezekiel's title for the future ruler (34:24; 37:25; chs. 44-48), kept apart from *śārîm* 'officials' (11:1) by `sar-and-nasi-officials-and-prince-ezekiel`. The source spells *leʾĕḵôl* with an unusual vowel and *waw* (*לֶאֱכָול*); this is reproduced from the Leningrad Codex, and no Ketiv/Qere is marked (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *leʾĕḵol-leḥem lip̄nê YHWH* 'to eat bread before YHWH' is a sacrificial meal (cf. Ex 18:12). *middereḵ ʾûlām haššaʿar* 'by the way of the porch of the gate' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse twice ('the prince ... shall sit in it to eat bread before Yahweh'; 'He shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate'). It reads the prince as the one person allowed to meet the creators, and the porch as an airlock where he was sterilized. The line renders *ʾûlām* 'porch' under the central Temple-plan entry.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֜נִי דֶּֽרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר הַצָּפוֹן֮ אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבַּיִת֒ וָאֵ֕רֶא וְהִנֵּ֛ה מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶפֹּ֖ל אֶל־פָּנָֽי׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me by the way of the north gate to the front of the house; and I looked, and behold — the glory of YHWH filled the house of YHWH; and I fell on my face.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh mālēʾ ḵəḇôḏ-YHWH ʾeṯ-bêṯ YHWH* 'and behold — the glory of YHWH filled the house of YHWH' (`kavod-yhwh`), as at 43:5. The prophet falls on his face, as at 1:28, 3:23 and 43:3.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהֹוָ֗ה בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם שִׂ֣ים לִבְּךָ֩ וּרְאֵ֨ה בְעֵינֶ֜יךָ וּבְאָזְנֶ֣יךָ שְּׁמָ֗ע אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אֹתָ֔ךְ לְכָל־חֻקּ֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וּלְכָל־תורתו [תּֽוֹרֹתָ֑יו] וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ לִבְּךָ֙ לִמְב֣וֹא הַבַּ֔יִת בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹצָאֵ֥י הַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: YHWH said to me, "Son of human, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I am speaking with you concerning all the statutes of the house of YHWH and all its laws; and set your heart on the entrance of the house, with all the exits of the sanctuary.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *twrtw* 'its law' / Qere *tôrōṯāyw* 'its laws' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *śîm libbəḵā* 'set your heart' (ASV 'mark well') is kept literally, as at 40:4. *ləmeḇôʾ habbayiṯ bəḵōl môṣāʾê hammiqdāš* 'on the entrance of the house, with all the exits of the sanctuary': the question of who may enter is the subject of the rest of the chapter. The speech runs from here to v 31.

paragraphs.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֶל־מֶ֙רִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רַב־לָכֶ֛ם מִֽכָּל־תּוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And say to the rebellious, to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel!

notes.official: *wəʾāmartā ʾel-meri* 'And say to the rebellious': *meri* 'rebellion' is used as a name for the house of Israel, as in 2:5-8. The oracle opens in single quotes ('Thus says the Lord YHWH') and runs to v 31 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`). *raḇ-lāḵem* 'Enough' (`toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: בַּהֲבִיאֲכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־נֵכָ֗ר עַרְלֵי־לֵב֙ וְעַרְלֵ֣י בָשָׂ֔ר לִהְי֥וֹת בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לְחַלְּל֣וֹ אֶת־בֵּיתִ֑י בְּהַקְרִֽיבְכֶ֤ם אֶת־לַחְמִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם וַיָּפֵ֙רוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֶ֖ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: When you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it — my house — when you offered my bread, the fat and the blood; and they broke my covenant, in addition to all your abominations.

notes.official: *bənê-nēḵār ʿarlê-lēḇ wəʿarlê ḇāśār* 'foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh' (cf. Jer 9:24-25; Deut 10:16). *ʾeṯ-laḥmî ḥēleḇ wāḏām* 'my bread, the fat and the blood'. *wayyāp̄ērû ʾeṯ-bərîṯî* 'and they broke my covenant' is the MT, with the foreigners as subject. The LXX, Syriac and Vulgate read *wattāp̄ērû* 'and you broke', which matches the second-person charge (NRSV 'You have broken'). The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; ASV 'they have broken').

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת קָדָשָׁ֑י וַתְּשִׂימ֗וּן לְשֹׁמְרֵ֧י מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֛י בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לָכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And you have not kept the charge of my holy things, but you have set them as keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.

notes.official: *wattəśîmûn ləšōmərê mišmartî bəmiqdāšî lāḵem* 'but you have set them as keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves'. The object is not expressed in the Hebrew. 'them' (the foreigners of v 7) is supplied because the English needs an object; the ASV construes *lə-* as the object marker ('ye have set keepers of my charge') (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: כֹּה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ כָּל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֗ר עֶ֤רֶל לֵב֙ וְעֶ֣רֶל בָּשָׂ֔ר לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֑י לְכָל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֕ר בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Thus says the Lord YHWH: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter my sanctuary — of any foreigner who is among the sons of Israel.

notes.official: *kol-ben-nēḵār ... lōʾ yāḇôʾ ʾel-miqdāšî* 'No foreigner ... shall enter my sanctuary', and the closing *ləḵol-ben-nēḵār ʾăšer bəṯôḵ bənê yiśrāʾēl* 'of any foreigner who is among the sons of Israel' restates the subject. The rule contrasts with the openness of Isa 56:3-7.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אִם־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽחֲקוּ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י בִּתְע֤וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּע֣וּ מֵֽעָלַ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

i18n.en: But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols — they shall bear their iniquity.

notes.official: *ʾaḥărê gillûlêhem* 'after their idols': *gillûlîm*, Ezekiel's polemical word (see 8:10). *wənāśəʾû ʿăwōnām* 'they shall bear their iniquity', the formula of liability (Num 18:23). The Levites who served at the high places are demoted to temple service (vv 11-14).

paragraphs.text: וְהָי֤וּ בְמִקְדָּשִׁי֙ מְשָׁ֣רְתִ֔ים פְּקֻדּוֹת֙ אֶל־שַׁעֲרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וּֽמְשָׁרְתִ֖ים אֶת־הַבָּ֑יִת הֵ֠מָּה יִשְׁחֲט֨וּ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַזֶּ֙בַח֙ לָעָ֔ם וְהֵ֛מָּה יַעַמְד֥וּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָֽׁרְתָֽם׃

i18n.en: They shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the house and ministering in the house; they shall slaughter the burnt-offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister to them.

notes.official: *pəquddôṯ ʾel-šaʿărê habbayiṯ* 'having oversight at the gates of the house'. *hēmmâ yišḥăṭû ʾeṯ-hāʿōlâ wəʾeṯ-hazzeḇaḥ lāʿām* 'they shall slaughter the burnt-offering and the sacrifice for the people' (`olah-burnt-offering`; `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). In Lev 1:5 the worshipper does the slaughtering.

paragraphs.text: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְשָׁרְת֤וּ אוֹתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עָוֺ֑ן עַל־כֵּן֩ נָשָׂ֨אתִי יָדִ֜י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

i18n.en: Because they ministered to them before their idols and became a stumbling-block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, declares the Lord YHWH, and they shall bear their iniquity.

notes.official: *lip̄nê gillûlêhem* 'before their idols' (see 8:10). *ləmiḵšôl-ʿāwōn* 'a stumbling-block of iniquity' (cf. 3:20; 7:19; 14:3-4). *nāśāʾṯî yāḏî ʿălêhem* 'I have lifted up my hand against them', the gesture of an oath (20:5-6, 15, 23).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־יִגְּשׁ֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לְכַהֵ֣ן לִ֔י וְלָגֶ֙שֶׁת֙ עַל־כָּל־קָ֣דָשַׁ֔י אֶל־קָדְשֵׁ֖י הַקְּדָשִׁ֑ים וְנָֽשְׂאוּ֙ כְּלִמָּתָ֔ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃

i18n.en: They shall not come near to me to serve me as priests, nor come near to any of my holy things, to the most holy things; but they shall bear their shame and their abominations that they have committed.

notes.official: *lōʾ-yiggəšû ʾēlay ləḵahēn lî* 'They shall not come near to me to serve me as priests'. *wənāśəʾû kəlimmāṯām* 'but they shall bear their shame' (`toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַבָּ֑יִת לְכֹל֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ וּלְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Yet I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all its service and for all that shall be done in it.

notes.official: *šōmərê mišmereṯ habbayiṯ* 'keepers of the charge of the house', the Priestly idiom of 40:45 and Num 3:7-8.

paragraphs.text: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י צָד֗וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְר֜וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ בִּתְע֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י הֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֵלַ֖י לְשָֽׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְעָמְד֣וּ לְפָנַ֗י לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

i18n.en: But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the sons of Israel went astray from me — they shall come near to me to minister to me, and they shall stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Lord YHWH.

notes.official:
*wəhakkōhănîm halləwiyyim bənê ṣāḏôq* 'But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok' (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`; cf. 40:46; 43:19). *ləhaqrîḇ lî ḥēleḇ wāḏām* 'to offer me the fat and the blood': the fat and blood are YHWH's portion (Lev 3:16-17; 7:23-27).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 44:15-16 ('They shall come near to me to minister unto me ... to offer unto me the fat and the blood ... they shall come near to my table') and reads the Levite priests as those who served the creators. The line renders the priestly vocabulary as the Priestly texts use it.

paragraphs.text: הֵ֜מָּה יָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֗י וְהֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֶל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י לְשָׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְשָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall come near to my table to minister to me, and they shall keep my charge.

notes.official: *wəhēmmâ yiqrəḇû ʾel-šulḥānî* 'and they shall come near to my table': either the wooden altar that 41:22 calls 'the table that is before YHWH', or the altar of burnt-offering (cf. Mal 1:7, 12). For the canon's quotation of this verse see the reception note at 44:15.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּבוֹאָם֙ אֶֽל־שַׁעֲרֵי֙ הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔ית בִּגְדֵ֥י פִשְׁתִּ֖ים יִלְבָּ֑שׁוּ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֤ה עֲלֵיהֶם֙ צֶ֔מֶר בְּשָֽׁרְתָ֗ם בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֛י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖ית וָבָֽיְתָה׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall put on linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them while they minister in the gates of the inner court and within.

notes.official: *bigḏê p̄ištîm yilbāšû* 'they shall put on linen garments': *pištîm* is linen, the same word as the 'flax' of the measuring cord (40:3). *wəlōʾ-yaʿăleh ʿălêhem ṣemer* 'and no wool shall come upon them'. Linen vestments are prescribed in Ex 28:39-43 and Lev 16:4. For the canon's quotation of vv 17-18 see the reception note at v 18.

paragraphs.text: פַּאֲרֵ֤י פִשְׁתִּים֙ יִהְי֣וּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔ם וּמִכְנְסֵ֣י פִשְׁתִּ֔ים יִהְי֖וּ עַל־מָתְנֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א יַחְגְּר֖וּ בַּיָּֽזַע׃

i18n.en: Linen turbans shall be on their heads, and linen breeches shall be on their loins; they shall not gird themselves with what causes sweat.

notes.official:
*paʾărê p̄ištîm* 'linen turbans' (ASV 'tires'), *ûmiḵnəsê p̄ištîm* 'linen breeches' (Ex 28:42). *lōʾ yaḥgərû bayyezaʿ* 'they shall not gird themselves with what causes sweat'. *yezaʿ* occurs only here (cf. *zēʿâ* 'sweat', Gen 3:19). The literal 'they shall not gird themselves in sweat' is rendered by its sense, as in the ASV ('[with any thing that causeth] sweat'), without brackets.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 17-18 ('they shall be clothed with linen garments ... they shall not gird themselves with any thing that causeth sweat') and comments that the smell of human sweat was disagreeable to the creators. The line renders the hapax by its accepted sense.

paragraphs.text: וּ֠בְצֵאתָם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֨ר הַחִיצוֹנָ֜ה אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִיצוֹנָה֮ אֶל־הָעָם֒ יִפְשְׁט֣וּ אֶת־בִּגְדֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֙מָּה֙ מְשָׁרְתִ֣ם בָּ֔ם וְהִנִּ֥יחוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בְּלִֽשְׁכֹ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְלָֽבְשׁוּ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם בְּבִגְדֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And when they go out into the outer court — into the outer court to the people — they shall take off their garments in which they minister and lay them in the holy chambers, and put on other garments, so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments.

notes.official: *ʾel-heḥāṣēr haḥîṣônâ* 'into the outer court' occurs twice in the MT ('into the outer court — into the outer court to the people'). The repetition is probably a dittography and is absent in the LXX and Syriac; it is kept, as in the ASV (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *wəlōʾ-yəqaddəšû ʾeṯ-hāʿām bəḇiḡḏêhem* 'so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments': holiness passes by contact, as at 42:14 (`qodesh-holy-chambers-and-garments-ezekiel-42-44`).

paragraphs.text: וְרֹאשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ וּפֶ֖רַע לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ כָּס֥וֹם יִכְסְמ֖וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: They shall not shave their heads, nor let their locks grow long; they shall only trim the hair of their heads.

notes.official: *wərōʾšām lōʾ yəḡallēḥû ûp̄eraʿ lōʾ yəšallēḥû* 'They shall not shave their heads, nor let their locks grow long' (cf. Lev 21:5; 10:6). *kāsôm yiḵsəmû* 'they shall only trim': *kāsam* occurs only here, 'clip, trim'.

paragraphs.text: וְיַ֥יִן לֹֽא־יִשְׁתּ֖וּ כָּל־כֹּהֵ֑ן בְּבוֹאָ֖ם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃

i18n.en: No priest shall drink wine when they enter the inner court.

notes.official: *wəyayin lōʾ-yištû kol-kōhēn* 'No priest shall drink wine' when serving in the inner court (Lev 10:9).

paragraphs.text: וְאַלְמָנָה֙ וּגְרוּשָׁ֔ה לֹֽא־יִקְח֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּ֣י אִם־בְּתוּלֹ֗ת מִזֶּ֙רַע֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה מִכֹּהֵ֖ן יִקָּֽחוּ׃

i18n.en: They shall not take for wives a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the seed of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest they may take.

notes.official: The marriage rule extends to all priests part of what Lev 21:7, 13-14 requires of the high priest. Ezekiel allows the widow of a priest.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־עַמִּ֣י יוֹר֔וּ בֵּ֥ין קֹ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹ֑ל וּבֵין־טָמֵ֥א לְטָה֖וֹר יוֹדִעֻֽם׃

i18n.en: They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and make them know the difference between the unclean and the clean.

notes.official: *bên qōḏeš ləḥōl ... bên-ṭāmēʾ ləṭāhôr* 'the difference between the holy and the common ... between the unclean and the clean': the priestly teaching office of Lev 10:10-11 (cf. 22:26, where the priests failed in it; 42:20).

paragraphs.text: וְעַל־רִ֗יב הֵ֚מָּה יַעַמְד֣וּ לשפט [לְמִשְׁפָּ֔ט] בְּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י ושפטהו [יִשְׁפְּט֑וּהוּ] וְאֶת־תּוֹרֹתַ֤י וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ בְּכָל־מוֹעֲדַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֔רוּ וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֖י יְקַדֵּֽשׁוּ׃

i18n.en: In a dispute they shall stand to judge; according to my ordinances they shall judge it; and they shall keep my laws and my statutes in all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my sabbaths holy.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *lšpṭ* 'to judge' / Qere *ləmišpāṭ* 'for judgment'; Ketiv *wšpṭhw* 'and they shall judge it' / Qere *yišpəṭûhû* 'they shall judge it'. The line's 'they shall stand to judge' coincides in wording with the Ketiv infinitive *lišpōṭ*; it renders the purpose that the Qere *ləmišpāṭ* 'for judgment' expresses, and the sense is the same. The second pair follows the Qere (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *wəʿal-rîḇ* 'In a dispute': the judicial role of the priests (Deut 17:8-9; 21:5). *wəʾeṯ-šabbəṯôṯay yəqaddēšû* 'and they shall keep my sabbaths holy'.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־מֵ֣ת אָדָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא לְטָמְאָ֑ה כִּ֣י אִם־לְאָ֡ב וּ֠לְאֵם וּלְבֵ֨ן וּלְבַ֜ת לְאָ֗ח וּלְאָח֛וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה לְאִ֖ישׁ יִטַּמָּֽאוּ׃

i18n.en: They shall not go near a dead human to become unclean; but for father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother, or for a sister who has not had a husband, they may make themselves unclean.

notes.official: *wəʾel-mēṯ ʾāḏām lōʾ yāḇôʾ ləṭāmʾâ* 'They shall not go near a dead human to become unclean': *ʾāḏām* here is a human being in general, rendered 'human' as in *ben-ʾāḏām*. The exceptions are close kin, as in Lev 21:1-3.

paragraphs.text: וְאַחֲרֵ֖י טָֽהֳרָת֑וֹ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים יִסְפְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And after his cleansing, they shall count seven days for him.

notes.official: *wəʾaḥărê ṭohŏrāṯô* 'And after his cleansing': the purification from corpse impurity takes seven days (Num 19:11-19), and Ezekiel adds a further seven.

paragraphs.text: וּבְיוֹם֩ בֹּא֨וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ יַקְרִ֖יב חַטָּאת֑וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

i18n.en: And on the day that he goes into the holy place, into the inner court, to minister in the holy place, he shall offer his sin-offering, declares the Lord YHWH.

notes.official: *yaqrîḇ ḥaṭṭāʾṯô* 'he shall offer his sin-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *nəʾum ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'declares the Lord YHWH'.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיְתָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְֽנַחֲלָ֔ה אֲנִ֖י נַֽחֲלָתָ֑ם וַאֲחֻזָּ֗ה לֹֽא־תִתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲנִ֖י אֲחֻזָּתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And it shall be to them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance; and you shall give them no possession in Israel: I am their possession.

notes.official: *wəhāyəṯâ lāhem lənaḥălâ ʾănî naḥălāṯām* 'And it shall be to them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance' is the MT. The Vulgate and many commentators read a negative ('they shall have no inheritance'), following the parallel clause and Num 18:20; the ASV smooths it as 'And they shall have an inheritance'. The MT is translated literally (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *ʾănî ʾăḥuzzāṯām* 'I am their possession' (Num 18:20; Deut 18:1-2).

paragraphs.text: הַמִּנְחָה֙ וְהַחַטָּ֣את וְהָאָשָׁ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה יֹֽאכְל֑וּם וְכָל־חֵ֥רֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָהֶ֥ם יִהְיֶֽה׃

i18n.en: The meal-offering and the sin-offering and the guilt-offering — they shall eat them; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.

notes.official: *hamminḥâ wəhaḥaṭṭāʾṯ wəhāʾāšām* 'The meal-offering and the sin-offering and the guilt-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`; ASV 'trespass-offering'). *wəḵol-ḥērem bəyiśrāʾēl* 'and every devoted thing in Israel': *ḥērem* is property irrevocably dedicated to YHWH, which falls to the priests (Lev 27:21, 28; Num 18:14).

paragraphs.text: וְרֵאשִׁית֩ כָּל־בִּכּ֨וּרֵי כֹ֜ל וְכָל־תְּר֣וּמַת כֹּ֗ל מִכֹּל֙ תְּרוּמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְרֵאשִׁ֤ית עֲרִסֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ תִּתְּנ֣וּ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן לְהָנִ֥יחַ בְּרָכָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And the first of all the first-fruits of everything, and every oblation of everything, of all your oblations, shall belong to the priests; and the first of your dough you shall give to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on your house.

notes.official:
*wərēʾšîṯ kol-bikkûrê ḵōl* 'And the first of all the first-fruits of everything': *rēʾšîṯ* is 'first' or 'best' (ASV 'the first'), and *bikkûrîm* are the first-ripe produce. *wəḵol-tərûmaṯ kōl* 'and every oblation of everything': *tərûmâ* is the portion set apart and lifted off for the sanctuary; it keeps the ASV 'oblation', the word Ezekiel's land-allotment chapters also use (45:1-7; 48:8-21) (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *wərēʾšîṯ ʿărîsôṯêḵem* 'the first of your dough' (Num 15:20-21; Neh 10:38 [ET 10:37]). *ləhānîaḥ bərāḵâ ʾel-bêṯeḵā* 'to cause a blessing to rest on your house': *bêṯeḵā* is singular, addressing each household.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('the first of your dough, ye shall give unto the priests, that the blessing may rest in thine house') and reads the dues as the provisioning of the creators with fresh produce. The line renders the cultic terms as the Priestly texts use them.

paragraphs.text: כָּל־נְבֵלָה֙ וּטְרֵפָ֔ה מִן־הָע֖וֹף וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לֹ֥א יֹאכְל֖וּ הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃ (פ)

i18n.en: The priests shall not eat anything that died of itself or was torn, whether bird or beast.'"

notes.official: *kol-nəḇēlâ ûṭərēp̄â* 'anything that died of itself or was torn' (Lev 22:8; cf. Ezek 4:14). The oracle and the speech of 44:5-31 close here.
